title: Polynomial time for a bounded loop
statement: Let $g,e,\mathrm{init},f$ be functions on bit strings, and suppose each of $g,e,\mathrm{init}$ is polynomial-time computable. Fix $a',k',b\in\mathbb{N}$, and suppose that for every bit string $w$ and natural number $i$, the length of the $i$-th iterate of $g$ at $w$ is at most $b(|w|+1)$. If, for every bit string $z$, concatenating $e(g^{[i]}(\mathrm{init}(z)))$ over $0\le i<a'(|\mathrm{init}(z)|+1)^{k'}+1$ gives $f(z)$, then $f$ is polynomial-time computable.
hypotheses_covered: Every iterate satisfies the stated length bound for all $w,i$
The specified finite concatenation equals $f(z)$ for every $z$
